chunks: But when He rescues them, they commit excesses in the land unjustly again. Your rebellion, O people, shall recoil back on your own selves. The joys of the world (are only ephemeral): You have to come back to Us in the end. We shall then inform you what you were doing.

key_terms.يَبْغُونَ: to commit excesses or act unjustly

ai.seo_question: What happened to the Israelites after God rescued them from Pharaoh according to Surah Yunus?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the psychological pattern of the Israelites, illustrating how divine grace often precedes a return to *bagh* (excess/arrogance), serving as a universal lesson for humanity. It underscores the transient nature of worldly *mata'* (enjoyment) compared to the eternal accountability of the Hereafter, a core theme in Shia theological reflections on human nature (*fitrah*) and divine justice.
